How we rate digital legacy tools

Every listing gets one of four verdict labels: Top pick, Good, Use with caution or Not recommended. We decide the label from the criteria below, using only the official documentation and pricing pages we cite.

What we check, by category

Vaults & password managers

  • Has a built-in emergency or legacy access feature
  • How safely access is released (wait time, owner can deny)
  • Plan required and price
  • Contact's experience (account needed, access levels)

Platform legacy settings

  • Whether a legacy or inactivity setting exists
  • What contacts actually receive
  • What is excluded
  • Cost and setup effort

Crypto inheritance

  • Keys stay in your control (self-custody)
  • A clear, documented path for heirs
  • Safeguards against early or fraudulent claims
  • Assets supported and price

Estate & document tools

  • Whether it creates legally valid documents, and where
  • Digital asset inventory and sharing
  • Price model
  • Fit for Australian users

What the labels mean

  • Top pick: does the legacy job well, with a documented, safe hand-over.
  • Good: works, with trade-offs you should know about.
  • Use with caution: limits or past issues mean it only suits some people.
  • Not recommended: lacks a working legacy feature today.

What we don't do

  • We don't publish numeric scores we can't derive from cited facts.
  • We don't guess prices or features. If a source doesn't state something, the table says "Not stated" or "Check official pricing".
  • We don't store your passwords, documents or personal data. Afterkeep is a directory only.

Sponsors can't buy a score

Paid placements are labelled Sponsored and use rel="sponsored" links. A sponsorship never changes a verdict label, a table fact or a ranking. See our independence policy.

Frequently asked questions

How does Afterkeep rate tools?

We assign one of four verdict labels from category-specific criteria, using only official sources that we cite on each page.

Can a company pay for a better rating?

No. Sponsored placements are labelled and never change a verdict, a fact or a ranking.

Why are there no star scores?

We only publish what we can back with a cited source, so we use clear labels instead of invented numbers.
